reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational framework integrates two core paradigms: capacity laws and stimulus laws. Capacity laws define inherent individual aptitudes (e.g., discriminanda, manipulanda, retentivity) that influence learning ease, modeled as additive contributions to a scalar learning outcome. Stimulus laws describe how material and presentation affect learning independently of capacity. These dual axes form a Cartesian product space where each point represents a unique learning scenario. The mathematical duality arises from treating capacity and stimulus as orthogonal dimensions: one defines agent capability, the other defines environmental affordance. Failure modes emerge when either axis fails—low capacity renders poor performance even with ideal stimuli, and poor stimulus design undermines even high-capacity learners. This structure supports a tensorial formulation of learning dynamics, where the joint distribution over capacity and stimulus determines expected learning outcomes. The system exhibits non-linear coupling when capacity and stimulus interact synergistically, e.g., high creativity (f) combined with structured presentation (S) yields exponential gains in inventive learning.
